title: Gazpromavia 9608
summary: A Sukhoi Superjet 100-95LR crashed on July 12, 2024, during a ferry flight from Lukhovitsy to Vnukovo, approximately 80 kilometers southeast of Moscow. The aircraft climbed to only 900 meters before beginning an uncontrolled descent. The investigation found that two angle-of-attack sensors had been installed with a five-degree deviation during maintenance, causing incorrect activation of the stall warning and protection systems.
probable_cause: Incorrect installation of angle-of-attack sensors during maintenance with approximately five-degree deviation, causing erroneous stall warning and protection system activation, resulting in uncontrolled descent and terrain impact.

factors.evidence: Two of the four angle-of-attack sensors installed with a deviation of approximately five degrees
An engineer at the Lukhovitsy Aviation Plant installed two AOA sensors with the deviation
Incorrect AOA readings caused elevator to automatically lower the nose and the aircraft to descend
Aircraft impacted with terrain in uncontrolled dive at 365 knots

events.text: Aircraft took off from Lukhovitsy Aviation Plant
Four minutes after takeoff aircraft made last radio contact, reached maximum altitude about 900 meters
Aircraft cruising with nose pitch angle 5-6 degrees; AOA sensors showing conflicting readings (10-11.5 vs 11-13.5 degrees)
First officer pulled nose up to nearly 14 degrees, autopilot disconnected; captain accelerated to 270 knots to arrest descent
At 4500 feet aircraft initiating to climb; crew disabled autothrottle, airspeed reached 308 knots triggering overspeed warning
At 3000 feet crew attempted to arrest descent but elevators did not respond; aircraft impacted wooded terrain at 365 knots
